normalized_statement: \begin{nonclaim}[Closure-only scope] The theory does not claim that raw substrates, provisional packages, public shadows, or undeclared probe spaces contain no needles. A no-needle theorem is asserted only for formed closures/layers with declared native probe families, null-mode legality, accepted predictive transport, adequacy or scoped nonclaim for dissolving probes, completed critical-pair ledgers, and all-six records. \end{nonclaim}
\begin{nonclaim}[Applications] The RH and Navier--Stokes sections are obligation maps. They identify what a proof must supply. They are not proofs of RH or Navier regularity. \end{nonclaim}

\begin{nonclaim}[Duality-confinement scope] The duality-confinement theorem in Section~\ref{sec:duality-confinement} does not claim that every involutive system confines objects to its fixed locus. It does not claim that invariant trace balance controls anti-invariant displacement. It does not claim that moving finite windows with no tail record prove exact confinement. It states the exact membrane records under which a fixed-locus confinement theorem follows. \end{nonclaim}

\begin{definition}[Packaged native currency] For an exact package \(\Gamma\), set \[ C_\Gamma=\Gamma^*C\Gamma,\qquad L_\Gamma=L\Gamma. \] If \(L_\Gamma\) is null-legal for \(C_\Gamma\), define \[ \K_{C,\Gamma}(L)=L_\Gamma C_\Gamma^\dagger L_\Gamma^*. \] \end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Packaged native currency]\label{def:main:packaged-currency}
For an exact package \(\Gamma\), set
\[
  C_\Gamma=\Gamma^*C\Gamma,\qquad L_\Gamma=L\Gamma.
\]
If \(L_\Gamma\) is null-legal for \(C_\Gamma\), define
\[
  \K_{C,\Gamma}(L)=L_\Gamma C_\Gamma^\dagger L_\Gamma^*.
\]
\end{definition}

\]

normalized_statement: \begin{definition}[Involutive object ledger] An involutive object ledger is a tuple \[ \mathfrak X=(X,J,\mu,\psi,Y,\mathcal J), \] where: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item \(X\) is a visible object/root/defect space; \item \(J:X\to X\) is an involution; \item \(\mu\) is a positive object ledger measure or finite positive weight system; \item \(Y\) is a real Hilbert response space; \item \(\mathcal J:Y\to Y\) is a linear isometric involution; \item \(\psi:X\to Y\) is an equivariant readout: \[ \psi(Jx)=\mathcal J\psi(x). \] \end{enumerate} Define \[ P_-:=\frac{I-\mathcal J}{2},\qquad \psi_-(x):=P_-\psi(x). \] The anti-invariant object ledger is \[ \mathsf A_X:=\int_X \psi_-(x)\psi_-(x)^*\,d\mu(x), \] interpreted in the finite-rank or trace-class sense whenever required. \end{definition}
raw_body:
\begin{definition}[Involutive object ledger]\label{def:main:involutive-ledger}
An involutive object ledger is a tuple
\[
\mathfrak X=(X,J,\mu,\psi,Y,\mathcal J),
\]
where:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \(X\) is a visible object/root/defect space;
\item \(J:X\to X\) is an involution;
\item \(\mu\) is a positive object ledger measure or finite positive weight system;
\item \(Y\) is a real Hilbert response space;
\item \(\mathcal J:Y\to Y\) is a linear isometric involution;
\item \(\psi:X\to Y\) is an equivariant readout:
\[
\psi(Jx)=\mathcal J\psi(x).
\]
\end{enumerate}
Define
\[
P_-:=\frac{I-\mathcal J}{2},\qquad \psi_-(x):=P_-\psi(x).
\]
The anti-invariant object ledger is
\[
\mathsf A_X:=\int_X \psi_-(x)\psi_-(x)^*\,d\mu(x),
\]
interpreted in the finite-rank or trace-class sense whenever required.
\end{definition}

normalized_statement: \begin{definition}[Separating anti-invariant readout] The anti-invariant readout separates the fixed locus when \[ \psi_-(x)=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\Fix(J) \] on the visible support of \(\mu\). It is quantitatively separating if for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is \(m(\varepsilon)>0\) such that \[ \dist(x,\Fix(J))\ge \varepsilon \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \|\psi_-(x)\|\ge m(\varepsilon). \] \end{definition}
raw_body:
\begin{definition}[Separating anti-invariant readout]\label{def:main:separating-readout}
The anti-invariant readout separates the fixed locus when
\[
\psi_-(x)=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\Fix(J)
\]
on the visible support of \(\mu\).  It is quantitatively separating if for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is \(m(\varepsilon)>0\) such that
\[
\dist(x,\Fix(J))\ge \varepsilon \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \|\psi_-(x)\|\ge m(\varepsilon).
\]
\end{definition}

normalized_statement: \begin{definition}[Carrier-side anti-invariant membrane] Let \(E\) be an exact packaged carrier with audit \(C\succeq0\) on its legal quotient and anti-invariant native probe family \[ L^-:E\to Y^-. \] The anti-invariant carrier currency is \[ \K^-:=L^- C^\dagger (L^-)^*, \] with null-mode legality required. A budget record is a positive operator \(\Theta^-\) with \[ \K^-\preceqq \Theta^-. \] A collapse ladder is a family of records \[ \K^-_n\preceqq B_n, \qquad \tr B_n\to0, \] or a defected version with \(B_n\) replaced by a bridge budget as below. \end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Carrier-side anti-invariant membrane]\label{def:main:anti-invariant-membrane}
Let \(E\) be an exact packaged carrier with audit \(C\succeq0\) on its legal quotient and anti-invariant native probe family
\[
L^-:E\to Y^-.
\]
The anti-invariant carrier currency is
\[
\K^-:=L^- C^\dagger (L^-)^*,
\]
with null-mode legality required.  A budget record is a positive operator \(\Theta^-\) with
\[
\K^-\preceqq \Theta^-.
\]
A collapse ladder is a family of records
\[
\K^-_n\preceqq B_n,
\qquad \tr B_n\to0,

normalized_statement: \begin{lemma}[Trace identity] If \(\mathsf A_X\) is trace-class, then \[ \tr\mathsf A_X=\int_X \|\psi_-(x)\|^2\,d\mu(x). \] Consequently \(\mathsf A_X=0\) if and only if \(\psi_-(x)=0\) for \(\mu\)-almost every visible object \(x\). \end{lemma}
raw_body:
\begin{lemma}[Trace identity]\label{lem:main:trace-identity}
If \(\mathsf A_X\) is trace-class, then
\[
\tr\mathsf A_X=\int_X \|\psi_-(x)\|^2\,d\mu(x).
\]
Consequently \(\mathsf A_X=0\) if and only if \(\psi_-(x)=0\) for \(\mu\)-almost every visible object \(x\).
\end{lemma}

normalized_statement: \begin{theorem}[Separation implies fixed-locus confinement] Assume the anti-invariant readout separates the fixed locus. If \[ \mathsf A_X=0, \] then \[ \mu(X\setminus\Fix(J))=0. \] If the ledger is finite with positive weights, every visible object with positive weight lies in \(\Fix(J)\). \end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Separation implies fixed-locus confinement]\label{thm:main:separation-confinement}
Assume the anti-invariant readout separates the fixed locus.  If

\[
\mu(X\setminus\Fix(J))=0.
\]
If the ledger is finite with positive weights, every visible object with positive weight lies in \(\Fix(J)\).
\end{theorem}

\]

\end{theorem}

normalized_statement: \begin{definition}[Exhaustive moving ledger] A finite-window or moving object ledger \(\mathsf A_{X,n}\) is exhaustive for a completed ledger \(\mathsf A_X\) if there are inclusions/transports \(\iota_n\) and tail operators \(T_n\succeq0\) such that \[ \mathsf A_X\preceqq \iota_n\mathsf A_{X,n}\iota_n^*+T_n. \] It is vanishing-exhaustive under bounds \(\mathsf A_{X,n}\preceqq B_n\) if \[ \tr(\iota_nB_n\iota_n^*)+\tr T_n\to0. \] \end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exhaustive moving ledger]\label{def:main:exhaustive-moving-ledger}
A finite-window or moving object ledger \(\mathsf A_{X,n}\) is exhaustive for a completed ledger \(\mathsf A_X\) if there are inclusions/transports \(\iota_n\) and tail operators \(T_n\succeq0\) such that
\[
\mathsf A_X\preceqq \iota_n\mathsf A_{X,n}\iota_n^*+T_n.
\]
It is vanishing-exhaustive under bounds \(\mathsf A_{X,n}\preceqq B_n\) if
\[
\tr(\iota_nB_n\iota_n^*)+\tr T_n\to0.
\]
\end{definition}

normalized_statement: \begin{theorem}[Exhaustive ledger squeeze] If \(\mathsf A_{X,n}\preceqq B_n\) and the moving ledger is vanishing-exhaustive for \(\mathsf A_X\), then \[ \mathsf A_X=0. \] Consequently, under readout separation, visible object mass is confined to \(\Fix(J)\). \end{theorem}

\[

\]

\end{theorem}

normalized_statement: \begin{definition}[Adequacy residual] The adequacy residual of $D$ relative to $L$ is \[ \boxed{\Xi_C(D\mid L)=K_{DD}-K_{DL}K_{LL}^\dagger K_{LD}.} \] \end{definition}
\begin{theorem}[Projection identity] \[ \boxed{\Xi_C(D\mid L)=T_D(I-P_L)T_D^*\succeq 0.} \] \end{theorem}
\begin{remark} The theorem says that $\Xi_C(D\mid L)$ is the dissolving readout after removing the part explained by native probes in the energy-dual geometry. \end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Optimal residual identity] For every linear map $A:Y\to Z$, \[ \boxed{(D_0-AL_0)C_0^{-1}(D_0-AL_0)^* =\Xi_C(D\mid L)+(A-A_*)K_{LL}(A-A_*)^*.} \] Consequently, $\Xi_C(D\mid L)$ is the Loewner-minimal residual currency among all attempts to factor $D$ through $L$. \end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exact adequacy] The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $\Xi_C(D\mid L)=0$; \item $D_0=A_*L_0$; \item there exists $A$ such that $D_0=AL_0$; \item $\ker L_0\subseteq \ker D_0$. \end{enumerate} \end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Adequacy promotion] \[ \boxed{K_{DD}\preceq A_*\Theta_YA_*^*+\Xi_Z.} \] In particular, if $\Xi_C(D\mid L)=0$, native anti-localization transfers exactly to the dissolving family through $A_*$. \end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Chain rule for adequacy residuals] \[ \boxed{\Xi_C(D\mid L^+)=\Xi_C(D\mid L)-K_{DM\mid L}K_{MM\mid L}^\dagger K_{MD\mid L}.} \] In particular, \[ \Xi_C(D\mid L^+)\preceq \Xi_C(D\mid L). \] \end{theorem}
\begin{corollary}[Same-family saturation] If $M=BL$ for some $B$, then \[ \Xi_C(D\mid[L;M])=\Xi_C(D\mid L). \] \end{corollary}
\begin{theorem}[Dissolving post-processing] For a response map $F:Z\to Z'$, \[ \boxed{\Xi_C(FD\mid L)=F\Xi_C(D\mid L)F^*.} \] \end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Native coarsening] For a native response map $A:Y\to Y'$, \[ \boxed{\Xi_C(D\mid AL)\succeq \Xi_C(D\mid L).} \] If $A$ is a faithful reparameterization on $\Ran L_0$, equality holds. \end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No-go NG3: packing / amplitude] For a bad set of size $\sim r^{3-d}$ and amplitude $\sim r^{-\alpha}$, the contribution to $\|\DBG u\|$ scales as $r^{(3-d)/2-\alpha}$. Amplitude suppression by packing alone requires $\alpha<(3-d)/2$; otherwise small-set sparseness does not control $\DBG$-amplitude, and the no-go forces a sector-matched amplitude bridge or paid tail-smallness record. \end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No-go NG4: sparse-shadow] Imported sparse or intense sets do not pay $\Omega_{\mathrm{bb}}$ (bad-cylinder / bad-geometry overlap) unless either the sparse field is sector-contained in the bad-bad / mismatch sector or a paid mismatch record $\Omega_{\mathrm{mm}}\succeq 0$ is supplied. \end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No-go NG5: marker-only] Triad markers, bad-overlap masks, and similar marker-only fields identify where and what class a defect lives in, but do not dominate the $\DBG$-amplitude without a quantitative bridge. Promotion from marker payload to $\Omamp$ requires an amplitude bridge supplied either by a new native probe family (\Cref{thm:ns:source-admission-recurrence}) or by a record-grade $M^{\mathrm{bb}}$ bound. \end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No-go NG6: metric-shadow] Weighted or Gevrey-flavored metrics that shrink the apparent residual do not control the fixed $\DBG$ readout unless the normalized metric still dominates the BG/BKM amplitude. Concretely, geometry inputs from Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg parabolic regularity or Constantin--Fefferman vorticity-direction geometry act as metric shadows, and a sector-matched amplitude bridge plus an explicit dominance constant and time gate must be supplied as a separate record. \end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No-go NG7: moving-window / derivative-stack support-only] Finite Littlewood--Paley windows or derivative-stack windows that are merely supported on moving sets do not promote to a completed carrier closure. Promotion requires either a finite-termination record, a fixed-ledger squeeze, or an exhaustive-ledger squeeze; moving-window data alone is theorem-grade insufficient. \end{theorem}

normalized_statement: \begin{definition}[Six refinement kinds] A refinement morphism's per-field annotations belong to one of six disjoint kinds: \textbf{A1} scope expansion (enlarging $\mathfrak S$ within a fixed scope chain); \textbf{A2} record-field expansion (adding admissible records to one of the registries); \textbf{A3} stage / refinement-axis growth (extending $\mathrm{Stage}$ by a new stage); \textbf{A4} constraint tightening (replacing a constraint by a strictly stronger one); \textbf{A5} morphism strengthening (replacing a morphism by a refinement of itself); \textbf{A6} carrier (probe / target) refinement (replacing $(H,q,Q)$ or a probe/target family by a finer version, with a declared projection map). \end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$\RefPreSB$ category] The category $\RefPreSB_{\mathfrak S}$ is the full category of PreSB carriers of scope $\mathfrak S$ with refinement morphisms. A \emph{refinement chain} is a directed diagram in $\RefPreSB_{\mathfrak S}$ indexed by a directed poset. \end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[$\RefPreSB$ is directed-cocomplete] The category $\RefPreSB_{\mathfrak S}$ has all directed colimits. Concretely, for a directed diagram $(\mathsf C_j,\rho_{jj'})$ with projections $p_{jj'}:\mathsf C_{j'}\to\mathsf C_j$ along reverse arrows, the colimit object $\mathsf C_\infty=\mathrm{colim}_j\mathsf C_j$ has record/scope data as the directed union of the corresponding $\mathsf C_j$ data, and carrier data as the inverse limit of compatible threads under the projections $p_{jj'}$. The construction is functorial and preserves PreSB-typing. \end{theorem}

normalized_statement: \begin{definition}[Asymptotic statuses] For a residual atom $a$ of a colimit object $\mathsf C_\infty=\mathrm{colim}_j\mathsf C_j$, the \emph{asymptotic statuses} extending AOR-8 are: \texttt{asymptotic\_budgeted} (there exists a uniform finite budget $B$ and a tail index $J_0$ with the per-stage cost bounded by $B$ for all $j\ge J_0$); \texttt{summable} (the per-stage costs are summable across the directed chain); \texttt{contractive} (the per-stage cost ratios tend to a constant strictly less than $1$); \texttt{eventual\_zero} (the per-stage cost is zero for all $j\ge J_0$ for some tail index $J_0$). \end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Asymptotic soundness] The four asymptotic statuses of \Cref{def:aor:asymptotic-statuses} satisfy the implication chain \[ \texttt{eventual\_zero} \Rightarrow \texttt{contractive} \Rightarrow \texttt{summable} \Rightarrow \texttt{asymptotic\_budgeted}. \] Each asymptotic status closes the colimit residual at level $\Dlimit$ without producing a fresh atom in the limit. Moreover, if every atom of $\mathsf C_\infty$ has an asymptotic status from this list and every finite stage $\mathsf C_j$ is in $\CascadeStableAOR_{\mathfrak S}$, then $\mathsf C_\infty\in\AOR_{\mathfrak S}$. \end{theorem}
